title: Pull Request Templates
learning_objectives: Explain the purpose of PR templates in maintaining code quality
Create a GitHub pull request template file
Design PR template sections (description, changes, testing, checklist)
Write clear PR descriptions that facilitate code review
Link PRs to issues using GitHub keywords (Closes, Fixes, Resolves)
Use PR templates consistently for all CatchBook PRs
Customize PR templates for different types of changes
Understand how PR templates integrate with team workflows
outline: Introduction: Why PR templates improve collaboration
Anatomy of a good PR description
GitHub PR template location and file naming (.github/pull_request_template.md)
Essential PR template sections: Overview, Changes, Testing, Screenshots
Optional sections: Related Issues, Breaking Changes, Deployment Notes
Writing the 'Why' and 'What': motivation and implementation summary
Checklist items: common quality gates (tests pass, docs updated, etc.)
Linking PRs to issues: Closes #123, Fixes #456, Resolves #789
PR template markdown formatting: headers, lists, code blocks
Multiple PR templates for different change types (feature, bugfix, docs)
Real-world examples from popular open-source projects
Hands-on: Create CatchBook PR template with standard sections
Hands-on: Open PR using template for README improvements
Hands-on: Customize template for CatchBook feature PRs vs bugfix PRs
outline_structure_notes: Sections 1-11 are conceptual/examples. Sections 12-14 are hands-on exercises.
checkpoint_placement_guidance: After section 5 (sections overview), after section 9 (markdown formatting), after section 11 (real-world examples), after final hands-on exercise (section 14).

catchbook_context.feature: PR template for all CatchBook feature development
catchbook_context.deliverable: GitHub PR template file committed to CatchBook repository

criteria: PR template file created in correct location (.github/pull_request_template.md)
Template includes essential sections (description, changes, testing, checklist)
PR opened using template with all sections completed
PR correctly links to related issue using GitHub keywords
Template markdown is well-formatted and readable
Demonstrate creating custom template for feature vs bugfix PRs

professor_constraints: Show PR template rendering in GitHub UI (split view: raw markdown vs rendered)
Demonstrate how template auto-populates PR description field
Provide 3-5 real PR descriptions from popular projects as examples
Emphasize template as guideline, not rigid requirement
Show how checklist items become interactive checkboxes in GitHub
Address 'template overhead' concern by showing long-term time savings
Connect PR template to code review process from P01-M02-L03
Use CatchBook feature examples for all template demonstrations
